findings.problem: for an .each case tp moves to the second call's paren and indent_end starts after it, so the first call's table is never indentation-checked and the title is read at the relocated tp: a stray backtick in U2's table swallows describe-level code up to a later .each row case and the span takes that case's id
findings.scenario: p1.py EB1: .tsx, row U5, it.each([[<kbd>`</kbd>, 1]])('U2 …') + beforeEach + it.each([// the backquote key: ` …])('U5 maps %s'); Edit of reset() in the beforeEach: fix PASS, base DENY; EB2 Edit of frozen unlisted U2 body: fix PASS, base DENY; no lift needed
findings.closure: EB1 and EB2 deny (a .each case whose first-call span holds another it/test call is refused, or the table is indentation-checked from m.end()); T9 (plain multi-line .each table) and T10 (tagged table) still pass.

findings.problem: indent_end reads raw lines, so a real multi-line template literal with lines at or below the call indent (column-0 markdown, YAML, inline snapshot at column 0) or an options-object third argument (`}, {`) makes the case bad and refuses every row Edit below it, no marker lifts it
findings.scenario: p2.py T1/T1b/T2/T3b and T4: Edit of row U2 under U1 holding such a template: fix DENY, base PASS
findings.closure: T1 and T2 pass, or the false positive is accepted and documented by the user (inherent to the dual check: a string-aware scan cannot keep the backtick swallow closed).

findings.problem: only the scanner-past-indentation direction is checked (the round-5 contract says the spans must agree); the Edit controls its call line's indentation, so de-indenting it stretches the indentation span to the describe close and the CW swallow passes
findings.scenario: p6.py/p7.py CW_deindent_call_line, CW_tab_call_line, then an Edit of the injected vi.spyOn beforeEach: fix PASS, base PASS
findings.closure: CW_deindent and CW_tab deny: the char span must end on the last non-blank line of the indentation span (two-direction agreement); T5, T6, T7, T12 and the wrapped-arrow form still pass.

findings.problem: the end-line conditions (ind == base, first char in )}]) are pinned by no case: mutants M04/M06/M09 survive all 100 scanner cases and each lets a case swallow a beforeEach, with or without a lift
findings.scenario: a4.py NL (.tsx, `# U2: r` only, single-line U2 with <kbd>`</kbd>, next base line beforeEach(() => reset()) // the ` key))): fix DENY, M04/M06 PASS; NL10: fix DENY, M04/M09 PASS
findings.closure: NL and NL10 (no lift) as LP cases, plus P7/P8 if the lift stays; each red under its mutant (M04, M06, M09).
